family.description: This family contains phosphate regulatory proteins including PhoU. PhoU proteins are known to play a role in the regulation of phosphate uptake. The PhoU domain is composed of a three helix bundle [[cite:PUB00031207]]. The PhoU protein contains two copies of this domain. The domain binds to an iron cluster via its conserved E/DXXXD motif.
family.name: PhoU domain

history.description: Curated24 observed edges for E. coli PhoU and M. smegmatis PhoU1/PhoU2 after exact reference/domain mapping and visual inspection of11 original figures. Four direct purified-system readouts and20 indirect cellular effects retain compound interventions, unequal probe doses, copy/context dependence, negative autokinase evidence and unresolved atomic mechanisms. Added five evidence ledgers and two open discussions. Family status IN_PROGRESS; regeneration and retained self-review follow. No publication or whole-family completion claimed.

Regenerate the effective record and retain the scientific self-review; no family-wide completion or publication claimed.

evidence.explanation: Transport Methods and Results plus visually inspected Figure7A show the induced deletion-versus-parent contrast. Figure7B bounds the abundance control; means and SD derive from three trials.

This is cellular uptake, not purified PstB ATPase inhibition. A12min accumulation result is reported without shown data and is not a second curated edge.

evidence.explanation: Figure5B dark QuadW curve is below the F194W curve; Methods and biochemical Results state the different masses, fitted values and retained probe substitution. Folding/solubility and combined-mutation alternatives remain explicit.

edges.mechanism: The QuadW preparation gives a smaller normalized Mn response than F194W across the inspected titration. Reported apparent Kd85.2+/-26.3uM is weaker than18.3+/-6.2uM; the paper uses94% confidence intervals. The intervention explicitly includes the changed protein load, so it is not a controlled effect of each residue alone.

causal_graphs.limitations: The direct endpoint is a biophysical fluorescence response, interpreted as apparent metal binding. It is not native in-vivo metal occupancy. Quad comparisons include unequal protein loads and preparation/solubility differences. The Methods QuadW residue list has a duplicated R201A; Table1 and construction define the four substitutions. The supplementary Mg curve was not inspected. E. coli ICP-MS does not establish iron binding.

record.description: This family contains phosphate regulatory proteins including PhoU. PhoU proteins are known to play a role in the regulation of phosphate uptake. The PhoU domain is composed of a three helix bundle [[cite:PUB00031207]]. The PhoU protein contains two copies of this domain. The domain binds to an iron cluster via its conserved E/DXXXD motif.

evidence.explanation: Figure5 probe/dose limits, Figure6 plasmid-versus-integrant distinction and Figure7 qualitative fractionation are retained. Unavailable supplementary Mg/SEC curves and the coelution condition discrepancy need inspection.

Separate AP, growth and BACTH results prevent a uniform loss-of-function claim. DCA/docking remains a hypothesis; Figure5B omits R148E. Figure2 medium discrepancy and exact fusion orientation/dose need resolution.

PhoU1/Pi alters net RegX3 phosphorylation without reducing SenX3 autophosphorylation. Direct Pi binding, a predicted alpha6 site and the balance of phosphotransfer versus phosphatase activities need discriminating biochemical tests.

discussions.notes: Recover supplements, verify constructs and matched protein concentrations, assay occupancy and isolated reaction rates, and retain negative/condition-dependent results. Do not draw metal-to-membrane-to-kinase arrows by joining distinct assays. Exact references and the access audit are retained under evidence/PF01895.
discussions.prompt: Resolve metal, phosphate and partner-interaction mechanisms without promoting reporter effects or models to atomic causal steps.
discussions.rationale: E. coli Mn-probe data and mycobacterial net RegX3 phosphorylation support distinct experimentally scoped effects. Neither establishes universal iron occupancy, direct Pi binding, a PhoU phosphatase active site, or inhibition of SenX3 autophosphorylation. Whole proteins carry two PF01895 repeats, and mutations can affect folding or abundance.

evidence.explanation: Whole-cell uptake is curated; additional growth, suppressor, mutant and long-term accumulation contexts remain unreviewed or reported without shown data.
Salmonella signaling/polyphosphate/virulence claims require full assay review and exact member mapping before graph transfer.
The final S. aureus publication replaces its preprint; conventional PhoU and PitR require separate identities and allele scopes, and reused experiments are not independent replications.

discussions.notes: Review mycobacterial2017 paralog phenotypes, conventional S. aureus PhoU, other structural homologs and persistence/virulence studies. Preserve imported identities/counters and the graphless state of unreviewed families. This is partial same-agent scientific curation, not exhaustive family coverage, independent endorsement or publication.
discussions.prompt: Extend the evidence review to other PhoU members and physiological contexts without merging PF01865/PitR into PF01895.
discussions.rationale: Three mapped reference proteins in two species do not establish the mechanism of24850 frozen proteins. E. coli combined PstSCAB/PhoU reconstitution and M. smegmatis PstB-deficient overexpression are different conditions, not interchangeable requirements or a controlled contradiction.
